models.equation_text: Conflict_{k,t} = β₁(Post × Mining Region × Covered Country)_{k,t} + η_{Mining Region×year} + η_{country×year} + η_k + ε_{k,t}.

fixed_effects.details: Cell fixed effects; Mining Region × Year joint fixed effects; Country × Year joint fixed effects. The paper notes that the fixed-effects structure subsumes the main effects of Post, Covered Country, and Mining Region, plus the Post × Covered Country and Covered Country × Mining Region terms.

evidence.quote: We include mining region × year
We include cell, mining region × year, and country × year fixed effects.
Thus, the main effects of _Post_, _Covered_ _Country_, and _Mining_ _Region_ are subsumed by our fixed effects’ structure.

Additionally, the _Post_ and _Covered_ _Country_ interaction term and the _Covered_ _Country_ and _Mining_ _Region_ interaction terms are subsumed by country × year and cell fixed effects, respectively.

estimation_procedure.description: Difference-in-difference-in-differences design: compare pre/post changes in conflicts between mining and nonmining regions in covered countries with the corresponding difference in noncovered countries. Post equals 1 after 2014 (2015–2019); the focal regressor is the triple interaction. No separate fits by group are reported.

evidence.quote: We employ a difference-in-difference-in-differences (DDD) research design in alignment with Section 1502’s sole application to covered countries and mining-related conflict mitigation.

Thus, we compare the pre-post difference in conflicts in covered countries’ mining regions and covered countries’ nonmining regions with the pre-post difference in conflicts in noncovered countries’ mining regions and noncovered countries’ nonmining regions.

scope.quote: To fill this void, we investigate whether and how Section 1502 successfully fulfills its goal of conflict mitigation.
But the regulation’s impact on conflict mitigation in the DRC and neighboring countries remains unclear.
Our paper re-examines the regulation’s effectiveness by focusing on the post-implementation period years—after issuers were mandated to submit CMDs in 2014.
In response to Dodd–Frank Act Section 1502, conflicts in the mining regions of the covered countries will be alleviated.

evidence.quote: The results show that the coefficient of interest is negative and significant, indicating that the probability of having at least one conflict in covered countries’ mining regions is 3.3 percentage points lower relative to other regions.

review_notes: Selected Table 5 column (1) is the LPM baseline; column (2) is the conditional fixed-effects Poisson robustness/count model and is outside this selected result family.

Scope decision: retain the PRIO-GRID conflict-effect DDD family at equation (3), Table 5 column (1). The introduction frames conflict mitigation as the unresolved effectiveness question after documenting responsible-sourcing and smelter-demand changes, and the authors describe the DDD analysis as the post-implementation conflict-effect design. H1 sourcing and smelter-demand regressions are substantial competing outcomes, but they estimate distinct upstream outcomes and supply no fitted inputs needed by this conflict regression; they are not dependencies. Exclude the separate count-model robustness in Table 5 column (2), parallel-trends/robustness analyses, institutional and price splits, and Eastern DRC follow-up.
